Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase. The umpires make their way out to the middle and so do the Namibia Under-19 fielders can be seen in a huddle before taking their field positions. Ryan Kamwemba and Panashe Taruvinga will open the batting for Zimbabwe. Jack Brassell to bowl the first over of the run chase. Let's play...
...THE RUN CHASE...

Right then, Zimbabwe Under-19 have the target well within their reach and it shouldn't be a tough task for them to chase it down. Namibia Under-19 will need some miracle to restrict them. Stay tuned as the run-chase is just around the corner.

Simbi is in for a chat for his brilliant spell. He says that he managed to bowl dots and kept it simple. Adds that they are happy with the score they need to chase and ends by saying that they are confident that they can win this.

So, Zimbabwe Under-19 have to chase a below-par target of 146 runs and it is surely not a difficult task. Have to say that Zimbabwe Under-19 were excellent with the ball. They spat fire from the get-go. They bowled very few loose deliveries and did not gave the Namibia batters any chance to settle in. Newman Nyamhuri was undoubtedly the pick of the bowlers as he was the one who ran over the Namibia top order and has four wickets in his bank! He bowled a barrage of short-pitched deliveries which garnered him the results. He finished his spell with a brilliant 4-fer by conceding just 23 runs. Ryan Simbi picked up three wickets and was equally effective. These two totally dented the batting order. But they were a bit sloppy in the field in the backend which helped Namibia to score some handy runs.

Namibia already had their back against the wall and their situation deteriorated further as none of their batters showed any intent to stitch partnerships and got out cheaply. The skipper Alexander Volschenk did try to contribute but soon perished despite of getting a start. Gerhard Van Rensburg also scored a handy 23 but just couldn't get going. The rest of the pack was sent packing on single-digit scores. Hanro Badenhorst played a fantastic hand of 39 runs. He was mature with his innings and showed great courage and helped Namibia to post 146. They managed to score 27 runs off the last three overs thanks to a crucial cameo of Hanro Badenhorst.
Short and on off, Hanro Badenhorst slaps it towards long off for a brace. Zimbabwe Under-19 end their innings for 146/8.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin! The umpires and the players stride out in the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Namibia's first followed by the national anthem of Zimbabwe. Done with the national anthems, and the players take their respective fielding positions now. Johannes De Villiers and Gerhard Van Rensburg will open up for Namibia Under-19. Anesu Kamuriwo comes to bowl. Let's go...

PITCH REPORT - Tino is at pitchside and he says that it is quite breezy and overcast today and the squares of the ground are not equidistant as it's 80m at one end and just 59, at the other. The pitch has been used before and it has something for the spinners. There is some fine grass in the middle and Zimbabwe Under-19 bowling first is the safe decision according to Scott Styris.
Alexander Volschenk says that it doesn't matter it's a good toss to lose. Says they have worked really hard and they had some tough outings but they will look to make a comeback in this game.

Matthew Schonken of Zimbabwe Under-19 won the toss and elected to bowl first. He says that there's a bit of grass on the deck and it can be easier to bat in the later half of the day. Obviously, it is a crucial game for them and says that they need to win this and further says that they are not thinking about it much further and taking match-by-match.

Namibia Under-19 (Playing XI) - Johannes De Villiers, Gerhard Van Rensburg, Johannes Visagie (WK), Zacheo Vuuren, Alexander Volschenk (C), Ben Brassell (In for Henry Van Wyk), Jack Brassell, Peter-Daniel Blignaut, Hanro Badenhorst, Woutie Niehaus, Junior Kariata
Zimbabwe Under-19 won the coin flip and they have elected to BOWL first.

Zimbabwe Under-19 are coming into the game after a crushing defeat of 225 runs against Australia. With Ronak Patel and Nathaniel Hlabangana leading the charge with bat, they're hungry for victory. However, Zimbabwe faces a hurdle with Kohl Eksteen's fitness in question. Can Anesu Kamuriwo and Newman Nyamhuri step up to fill the gap in the bowling attack? Zimbabwe holds a perfect record against Namibia in Youth ODIs, but they have lost their four matches out of the previous five games. So, the tension is palpable as these young stars clash on the field. We shall find out later in the match as the Toss and the teams are just around the corner.

Greetings and a warm welcome to our coverage of Match 20 in Group C of the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2024! Today, it's all or nothing as Zimbabwe Under-19 takes on Namibia Under-19 at the Diamond Oval in Kimberley in a virtual knockout battle! The Top 3 from each Pool will qualify for the Super Six phase of the competition. From Pool C, Australia and Sri Lanka have almost qualified ahead and now it's going to be either Namibia Under-19 or Zimbabwe Under-19. Namibia's resilience in their clash with Sri Lanka was commendable as they had the upper hand after the first innings, restricting them to a paltry 133. Despite the setback, they showed flashes of brilliance, particularly through the remarkable bowling performances of Johannes de Villiers and Zacheo van Vuuren, who picked three and four wickets respectively. They are itching to redeem themselves. But the batters need to step up and try to play all the allotted 50 overs.
